messages:
marie: Heads-up 0: release stalled. publish blocked by regendiff in generated types for the JS SDK. Looks like a pure ordering churn, no semantics changed.

ci-bot: CI: release/sdk-js #704 failed  regendiff detected: packages/js-sdk/src/gen/types.ts

marie: regendiff excerpt:
```
- export type User = { id: string; email?: string; name?: string }
+ export type User = { name?: string; email?: string; id: string }
```

ken: ugh, ordering-only diffs again. This will bump the release stamp and force a patch release even though behaviour didn't change.

elaine: quick fix ideas: (A) normalization step post-regen to stable-sort keys, (B) pin codegen & typegen versions across workspaces, (C) tweak release-stamp to ignore diffs that match a pure-ordering regex.

sam: for immediate unblock, (A)+(B) together worked for previous cut. Normalizer removes noise; pin prevents future binary drift. (C) is riskier but worth an RFC.

marie: I opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/704 that adds tools/normalize-gen.ts and pins @redwood/codegen to 3.4.4 in package.json. Also added a regen-idempotency CI job that runs regen twice.

ken: small nit: move normalize script under scripts/ and add a comment explaining it only affects generated files. We should not accidentally normalize handwritten sources.

elaine: long-term: RFC to change release-stamp semantics so that generator-only reorders don't auto-bump semver. We should require a non-generated diff or an explicit CHANGELOG entry to bump. Product needs to sign off.

sam: +1. Another follow-up: eng-ml should add a deterministic key ordering pass inside typegen so consumers don't need local normalizers. That reduces accidental churn for everyone.

marie: CI for PR #704 is green, merging now to unblock the release.

ci-bot: CI finished: all checks passed for PR #704.

marie: Merged and retriggered release pipeline. Publish step succeeded, js-sdk v3.1.5 published.

ken: filing INF ticket to track RFC and engine work: INF-2009. I'll draft the release-stamp proposal and loop in product.

elaine: thanks team. Leaving this thread open until RFC is in review. :white_check_mark:
